title: Prove the seams of SC-116 hold
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: After Stop on the stalled-SMB rig and the hung-cloud rig, the panel has no row for the folder Stop cut short or for unreached folders, and folders that failed before Stop are listed once each — shown by a window case on the published exe on each rig, reading the panel rows through the schema-1 report: partial

C2: The panel's reason is the reason of the read that failed: a folder that refused the last-access open and was then held without read sharing shows 'in use by another program', not 'access denied'; a folder that failed partway on the SMB rig shows 'only partly read' with 'network or share error' — window cases on a prepared temp folder and on the SMB loopback rig: partial

C3: On a whole C:\ scan as an ordinary user, panel row count equals the engine's Unreadable.Count, no row is a folder listed in full (including the ~306,000 refused last-access opens), and every row's reason is non-empty — a recorded, non-elevated run of the published net10 exe that compares schema-1 panel rows with Unreadable.Count and the tree's fully-listed state: missing

C4: 'Show in Explorer' on a panel row for a folder the user cannot open, at ~300 and ~1000 characters, opens its readable parent with that leaf selected, with no error and no elevation prompt — a window case that invokes the row action and checks the Explorer folder and selection by leaf Name through Shell.Application: partial

N-005, N-006, R-002 and W-001 change this PC's state or take its desktop: they add an SMB client mapping, register a cloud sync root, open real Explorer windows, and run a minutes-long C:\ scan. SL-088's validation marked such cases as runs for a person, but this slice's spikes ran every one of them unattended. May the build and validate stages run them here, or must a person run them? Until that is decided, the engine cannot discharge the obligations for C1, C3 and C4 on its own.

The cloud half of C1 may have no ending that lights the control. If the error-completion release also fails to put the cut-short folder in the list without Stop (as provider kill and the cldflt timeout already fail to), is C1's cloud half met by 'no row, and the platform never produces one', or should it be re-scoped?
No designer disagreed with another: there was one proposal. The items below are placements review may want to argue, not settled contests.

The rows dump lives in the test hook, read by reflection over UnreadableList's items. The alternative is a hidden App flag. The hook was chosen so the shipped exe never writes paths and the proof reads the panel, not the record.
C2's SMB half is folded into N-005's b row rather than given its own case.
The menu stays labelled 'Open in Explorer', while criterion 4 says 'Show in Explorer'.
C4 is two new steps in R-002 rather than a new case, R-003.
Code review m2's census inversion (O-036). Its obligation is waived and carried to SC-135, and this sending-back said to change no other test content.

Code review m2 (O-036, carried to SC-135): AppArgumentTests' census misses hand-quoting written with doubled quotes, string concatenation, or a command line built in a variable earlier. The review's fix inverts the census: every Start-App or Invoke-App call must either pass an array literal or call Format-AppArgument on that line. Its three proposed must-fire plants are still to be added.

O-036 not done: Not built. This obligation is waived and carried to SC-135 on the backlog. The code review's m2 decision still says accepted-pending, but this sending-back says to change no other src, test or fitness.yaml content. The census in `AppArgumentTests` therefore still catches only backtick-escaped hand-quoting.

drift: eng/rules-harness/plants.json `_note` still ends 'F36-F40 and P28-P31 are expectations written at SL-089's build, which no harness run has recorded yet.' This build's harness run recorded them (builder: 102 rows, 102 AS-RECORDED, exit 0; my run of 6 of them agreed). The note's convention for other slices (e.g. SL-095's 'recorded by SL-095's build run of the harness (--only S14-S26: 13 AS-RECORDED, exit 0 ...)') is to name the run, so the sentence should say SL-089's build run recorded them.

not reached: This attempt re-ran no real-contact case. The N-005, N-006, T-009, R-002 and W-001 results are attempt 1's at f9c303e, carried because nothing they read changed.

critique missed: The design and its 16 findings never asked what argv the app receives for the criterion's own literal root `C:\` when it goes through Invoke-HookedRun/Start-App. The launch line was hand-quoted without doubling a trailing backslash. The app got `C:" --report <file>`, report mode never started, and W-001 would hold a window open for 1200 s. eng/read-window.ps1:52 and CommandLine.RootArgument already encode the rule.

code-review missed: Nine plant rows (F36-F40, P28-P31 in eng/rules-harness/plants.json) anchored on a cut-off prefix of WindowReport.cs:276. harness.py:358-362 places a row only on a whole-line match, so none was placed or judged and the harness exited 1. The review passed it on laps 1-4. A check would be to run `harness.py --only F36,P28` and confirm AS-RECORDED, or to assert that each anchor matches exactly one whole stripped line.

critique missed: The design named the new held-folder window case T-008. Q-151 already refers to a T-008 (the 0xE0434352 exit launches), so the id was likely taken. The build shipped it as T-009, and the obligations (O-009, O-018) cite T-009. Inferred from Q-151, not from reading WindowCases.ps1: the design never checked the case ids it was allocating.

still unknown: Does a whole-C:\ W-001 run hold on this PC (non-elevated, SL-095 precaution on)? That means rows = core.unreadable = header N, no code-5 row that opens, the header's ', not scanned (M)' suffix parsed on a whole drive, and pool growth inside the 0.5 GB per-run guard. The notScanned branch has only run on C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows.

still unknown: Can a real cloud provider (OneDrive, or any provider other than tests/CfProvider) make cldflt return an error for a folder listing? Q-177's platform-limit verdict assumes the three endings are all a real provider can produce, and only tests/CfProvider on Windows 11 26200 was measured.

still unknown: Is the b-row code 59 from the client-side failpoint FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING=b|3|59 what a real SMB server drop gives through the app? The engine-level spike saw raw 64/121 under Cancel and 59 without Cancel. The app-level case injects 59 and states so. This matches the existing Q-150 on whether a real mid-listing error reaches DirectoryReader as a Win32 code.

went wrong: The plants.json anchor defect cost a whole extra cycle (build #4, code-review #5, validate #3) for nine anchor strings. Build #2 discharged O-021 on the strength of a Fact that tests the pattern, while the rule's real plant rows had never been placed. Code review passed it four times and said so itself. Validate was the only stage that ran the harness.

went wrong: The documented owner command `-Root C:\` would not have produced a report: W-001 would have waited its full 1200 s with a window open on the person's desktop. The design, 3 critique rounds and build #2 all missed it, and code review found it by measurement. The fix touched 15 launch sites across WindowCases.ps1 and HookCases.ps1 and added a 10-root corpus.

went wrong: The fix's own guard was unsound when first written. The AppArgumentTests census (AppArgumentTests.cs:22) matches only backtick-escaped quotes, so doubled-quote, concatenated and earlier-variable hand-quoting pass it (code-review m2). That is the same 'checker passes without the thing it names' pattern the project has hit before. It was waived to SC-135, so the guard stays partial.

went wrong: The design was a single proposal, clipped at 20,000 characters when handed to composition, and written before Q-176 and Q-177. The critique did the design's work: 16 findings, 9 major. They included a hook that does nothing without a stop mode, an un-twinnable rule 2, a kill that leaves an SMB mapping, a cloud release that cannot light its control, and an unattended C:\ scan that Q-176's own basis excludes.

went wrong: A large share of the pass counts is waiting, not rework. Critique #1 was stopped by a person, critique #2 left 16 findings waiting, and design #1 and build-check #1 halted on open questions or a partial survey. Those were answered by a model while the owner was away and are counted as untriaged in the gates' precision. Build #1 was halted by the machine guard (kernel +0.56 GB, two acting runs overlapping). The record does not say which run grew the pool, so the cause is unattributed.

went wrong: Criterion 3 was not discharged. Validate passed with 3 of 4 criteria MET and C3 carried as 'a person's run'. Validate #3 also re-ran no real-contact case and rests on attempt 1's runs at f9c303e. That is defensible because only plants.json changed since, but this slice's real-contact proof is one lap old.

went wrong: Build commit f9c303e stopped tracking the 45 `.taad-scratch/` files that SL-095's merge had committed, and neither the builder's account nor its declared deviations mention it. Merging SL-089 removes them from uat. Their copies under docs/design/SL-095-runs/ stay, and no SL-095 record cites a `.taad-scratch` path.

caused_by.reason: 1 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-034), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-034 (fix): M1 (major): W-001 passes -Root to the app through Invoke-HookedRun and Start-App, which quote it without doubling a trailing backslash. With the root the design, the record and the case's own error text name for criterion 3 (`-Root C:\`), the command line becomes `"C:\" --report "<file>"`. Windows splits that into one argument, `C:" --report <file>`. App.OnStartup finds no `--report` and starts in interactive mode with a bogus root. No report is written, and W-001 waits its full 1200 s with the window open on the person's desktop, kills the app, and fails 'a report was written'. The owner's criterion-3 run, the only way C3 can be discharged, cannot produce c-drive-run.json as written. The project already knows this rule: eng/read-window.ps1:52 doubles a trailing backslash ('C:\ would arrive as C:"'), and CommandLine.RootArgument documents the same escaping. Measured here: CommandLineToArgvW splits W-001's command line for C:\ into the one argument above. A 20 s launch of the published exe with `"C:\Windows\Logs" --report` exited 0 and wrote its report; the same with `"C:\Windows\Logs\"` never exited and wrote nothing. Double a trailing backslash before the root reaches argv, as read-window.ps1:52 does. Do it once in Invoke-HookedRun, or in Start-App's root argument, so every hooked case gets it: `$root -replace '(\\+)$', '$1$1'`. Then prove it with a W001OracleTests-style or C-013-style check: a rows-mode run of a temp root given with a trailing backslash writes its report and dump. Corpus rows: `C:\`, `<tempdir>\`, `C:` (Core's LongPath already repairs it to C:\), and a root without a trailing backslash. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. M1 is one member of "a root ending in a backslash handed to the app's argv undoubled" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-089/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close. Bound the class by who produces its members, not by every exotic spelling. Answer this obligation with `corpus`: the corpus's path from the repository root. It is not discharged without one.

caused_by.reason: validation partial this build: Checked the defect in the tree myself; it is real and this slice wrote it. eng/rules-harness/plants.json lines 151–159 hold SL-089's nine rows for rule 'TheWindowReportReadsOnlyTheFailedFolderCount (*.cs)': F36, F37, F38, F39, F40 (expect fire/fire) and P28, P29, P30, P31 (expect quiet/quiet). Each is op insert-after on src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs with anchor "byte[] json = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(report". harness.py:358-362 places a row only where `plain(line).strip() == anchor`, so it has to match a whole stripped line. WindowReport.cs:276 is the full line `byte[] json = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(report, new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true });`, so the anchor can never match. All nine rows are PLANT-BROKEN and the Q-027 harness exits 1. `git log -S '"id":"F36"'` shows the rows came in with 47d7154 (SL-089 WIP), main has none of them, and the working tree has no uncommitted change to plants.json or WindowReport.cs. These rows were never applied, so the rule's fire and quiet cases that O-021's fix requires have never actually been exercised by the harness. The validator also ran a diagnostic on a gitignored copy with the full-line anchor: 9/9 AS-RECORDED and harness exit 0. That points to an anchor-only fix, but I took that result from the report and did not re-run it. BUILDER'S JOB: (1) In eng/rules-harness/plants.json, change the "anchor" of F36, F37, F38, F39, F40, P28, P29, P30 and P31 to the exact stripped text of WindowReport.cs:276, which is `byte[] json = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(report, new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true });`. Keep every row's text, expect and note as they are. Escape it as JSON needs; no quotes need escaping here. (2) Run `C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Roaming\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe eng/rules-harness/harness.py --engine-root C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend` on the real plants.json, not a copy. It must exit 0 with 102 rows AS-RECORDED and 0 stray hits, with F36–F40 firing in both xUnit and Fitness and P28–P31 quiet in both. (3) Run eng/rules-parity.ps1 and Fitness check again so they still AGREE and hold. Change no other src, test or fitness.yaml content. The slice was planned to change no src, and the rule itself is not in question. Everything else in this validation stands and is not part of this job: the real-contact runs of N-005, N-006 (under Q-177), T-009, R-002, W-001 on three bounded roots, C-013, WindowMutants, the default suite at 559/562 with the 3 Q-190 last-access failures that predate this slice, and the clean leftover state. The whole-C:\ W-001 run remains the person's to give.
